name: Input Capture
description: Adversaries may use methods of capturing user input to obtain credentials or collect information. During normal device usage, users often provide credentials to various locations, such as login pages/portals or system dialog boxes. Input capture mechanisms may be transparent to the user (e.g. [Keylogging](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1417/001)) or rely on deceiving the user into providing input into what they believe to be a genuine application prompt (e.g. [GUI Input Capture](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1417/002)).

telemetry.name: API Calls
telemetry.description: Instrumented mobile API calls and results relevant to an application behavior.
telemetry.collection_focus: Instrument selected APIs in the owned test app or approved research build; log caller, API, sanitized argument class and return status.

providers.name: Android logcat
providers.scope: Permitted logs from a consented test device/emulator; output depends on build, permissions and instrumentation.

providers.name: Android dumpsys
providers.scope: Point-in-time service/package state on an authorized development device.

providers.name: Instrumented test application
providers.scope: Own-app permission, API and state callbacks; not universal visibility into other apps.

configuration: Use a disposable emulator or owned development device with approved debugging. Record OS/API level, app version and instrumentation privileges.
Collect only relevant logcat buffers/tags and service snapshots; add explicit own-app instrumentation for events absent from OS logs.
Forward sanitized logs and compare before/after state. Remove test data and revoke debugging access after the lab session.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Android tooling does not imply iOS coverage. Standard mobile apps cannot observe all other apps or protected OS internals; MDM status is not full API, filesystem or content telemetry.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Per owned device, app version and permission state: unexpected API/permission changes, background activity and network destinations. OS privacy restrictions and emulator differences limit observability.

telemetry.name: Network Traffic Flow
telemetry.description: Connection/flow summaries such as endpoints, duration, byte counts and transport.
telemetry.collection_focus: Collect Zeek conn.log, Suricata flow events or exporter equivalents, including observation point and sampling settings.

providers.name: Zeek
providers.scope: Connection and protocol metadata from traffic visible to the sensor.

providers.name: Suricata EVE
providers.scope: Configured flow, alert, DNS, HTTP, TLS and protocol records.

providers.name: AWS VPC Flow Logs
providers.scope: IP traffic metadata alternative; no packet payload or DNS answer history, and some traffic is not logged.

configuration: Use an authorized lab TAP/SPAN, virtual mirror or gateway interface. Define which traffic crosses it; avoid assuming visibility into every segment.
Enable the required Zeek analyzers or Suricata EVE event types. Export logs with sensor identity, clock synchronization and flow correlation identifiers.
Monitor capture loss, truncation and exporter sampling. Capture payload only with approval and restrictive retention; encryption normally prevents plaintext inspection.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Flows are not packet payloads. NAT, asymmetric routes, encryption, missing mirrors and sampling can hide attribution or content. A destination connection alone does not prove malicious intent.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Per source and observation point: connection rate, destination-host/port fan-out, response/failure ratio and previously unseen destinations. Compare equivalent time windows; separate authorized scanners, NAT and sampling effects.

telemetry.name: Permissions Request

telemetry.collection_focus: Correlate own-app request/callback instrumentation with the consented test-device prompt. A request callback alone does not prove a prompt appeared (for example, a previously denied permission).

analytics.name: Analytic 1825
analytics.guidance: For Android, detect Input Capture by correlating analyst-visible device/network evidence and management state; use streaming or batched telemetry only where the documented collector is deployed. Correlate API Calls via Application Vetting / Instrumented Dynamic Analysis [Dynamic API/runtime trace: AccessibilityEvent.TYPE_VIEW_TEXT_CHANGED received by listener_app NOT IN $AccessibilityAllowList$]; Network Traffic Flow via Android Enterprise Network Logging / Enterprise VPN [DevicePolicyManager.retrieveNetworkLogs(): DnsEvent / ConnectEvent; VPN flow metadata]; Permissions Request via Android Enterprise DPC / Application Vetting [DevicePolicyManager.getPermissionGrantState(); PackageManager manifest/requested-permission review]. Alert on a sequence or state change inconsistent with the device/app baseline, approved management policy, or expected user workflow; do not infer unobserved API calls, file/process activity, or payload content from management state alone.

tuning.description: Approved assistive tech, screen readers, approved IME apps. Keep minimal. Derive from MDM catalog.
Banking, auth, enterprise SSO, email app packages. Derive from MDM app catalog by data tier.
Default 10KB — keystroke logs are small but high-value. Tightening: 1KB.

log_sources.name: mobile:DynamicAnalysis
log_sources.channel: Dynamic API/runtime trace: AccessibilityEvent.TYPE_VIEW_TEXT_CHANGED received by listener_app NOT IN $AccessibilityAllowList$

analytics.name: Analytic 1826
analytics.guidance: For iOS, detect Input Capture by correlating analyst-visible device/network evidence and management state; use streaming or batched telemetry only where the documented collector is deployed. Correlate Application State via Apple MDM [InstalledApplicationList / ManagedApplicationList]; Network Traffic Flow via Apple Network Extension / Enterprise VPN [NEFilterFlow / per-app VPN / secure-web-gateway flow metadata]; Permissions Request via Application Vetting [Code-signing entitlements and Info.plist privacy usage-description keys]. Alert on a sequence or state change inconsistent with the device/app baseline, approved management policy, or expected user workflow; do not infer unobserved API calls, file/process activity, or payload content from management state alone.

tuning.description: IT-approved keyboard bundle IDs. Keep minimal.
Known cloud sync endpoints for each approved keyboard vendor.
Default 2 packets/sec — matches human average typing rate. Derive from keystroke baseline measurement.
Default 300s sustained — confirms ongoing capture vs one-time sync.

software.name: Phenakite
software.description: [Phenakite](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S1126) has used phishing sites for iCloud and Facebook if either of those were used for authentication during the chat sign up process.(Citation: fb_arid_viper)

references.description: Flossman, M., Scott, M. (2021, April). Technical Paper // Taking Action Against Arid Viper. Retrieved November 17, 2024.

software.name: CherryBlos
software.description: [CherryBlos](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S1225) has captured victims' credentials through predefined fake activities.(Citation: TrendMicro_CherryBlos_July2023)

references.description: Trend Micro Research. (2023, July 28). Related CherryBlos and FakeTrade Android Malware Involved in Scam Campaigns. Retrieved March 28, 2025.

mitigations.name: Use Recent OS Version
mitigations.description: The `HIDE_OVERLAY_WINDOWS` permission was introduced in Android 12 allowing apps to hide overlay windows of type `TYPE_APPLICATION_OVERLAY` drawn by other apps with the `SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW` permission, preventing other applications from creating overlay windows on top of the current application.(Citation: Android 12 Features)

references.description: Google. (2022, April 4). Features and APIs Overview. Retrieved April 5, 2022.

mitigations.name: User Guidance
mitigations.description: Users should be wary of granting applications dangerous or privacy-intrusive permissions, such as keyboard registration or accessibility service access.

mitigations.name: Enterprise Policy
mitigations.description: When using Samsung Knox, third-party keyboards must be explicitly added to an allow list in order to be available to the end-user.(Citation: Samsung Keyboards) An EMM/MDM can use the Android `DevicePolicyManager.setPermittedAccessibilityServices` method to set an explicit list of applications that are allowed to use Android's accessibility features.

references.description: Samsung. (2019, August 16). 3rd party keyboards must be whitelisted.. Retrieved November 17, 2024.
